questions.q: Which of the following statement is correct for the function $g ( \alpha )$ for $\alpha \in R$ such that~$g\left(\alpha\right) = {∫}_{\pi6}^{\pi3}\dfrac{\sin^{α}x}{\cos^{α}x + \sin^{α}x}dx$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$g\left(\alpha\right) = {∫}_{\pi6}^{\pi3}\sin^{α}x \left(\sin^{α}x + \cos^{α}x\right)dx \ldots \left(i\right)$

$g\left(\alpha\right) = {∫}_{\pi6}^{\pi3}\cos^{α}x \left(\sin^{α}x + \cos^{α}x\right)dx \ldots \left(ii\right)$

Adding~ \left($1\right) + \left(2\right)$

$2g\left(\alpha\right) = \dfrac{π}{3} - \dfrac{π}{6} = \dfrac{π}{6}$

$⇒ g\left(\alpha\right) = \dfrac{π}{12}

Which is constant and an even function.

$

Put $x = \dfrac{π}{4}$~

${ϕ}^{'} ( \dfrac{π}{4} ) = \dfrac{- 1}{2\left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right)3 / 2} \times0 + \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{π}} \left(4\sqrt{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} -3{ϕ}^{'} ( \dfrac{π}{4} )\right)$

$⇒ \sqrt{\dfrac{π}{4}}{ϕ}^{'} ( \dfrac{π}{4} ) +3{ϕ}^{'} ( \dfrac{π}{4} ) =4$

$⇒ {ϕ}^{'}\left(\dfrac{π}{4})\left($3 + $\sqrt{\dfrac{π}{4}}\right) =$4$

$⇒ {ϕ}^{'}\left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) = \dfrac{8}{6 + \sqrt{\pi}}$

$

questions.solution:
$I = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left[2x - \left|3x^{2} - 3x - 2x + 2\right| + 1\right]dx$

$I = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left[2x - \left|\left(3x - 2\right)\left(x - 1\right)\right|\right]dx + {∫}_{0}^{1}1dx$

$I = {∫}_{0}^{23}\left[\left(2x - \left(3x^{2} - 5x + 2\right)\right)\right]dx + {∫}_{23}^{1}\left(2x + \left(3x^{2} - 5x + 2\right)\right)dx + 1$

$I = {∫}_{0}^{23}\left[- 3x^{2} + 7x - 2\right]dx + {∫}_{23}^{1}\left(3x^{2} - 3x + 2\right)dx + 1$

Let~${I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{23}\left[- 3x^{2} + 7x - 2\right]dx$

The graph of~$y = - 3x^{2} + 7x - 2$~and~

${I}_{2} = {∫}_{23}^{1}\left(3x^{2} - 3x + 2\right)dx$

So~${I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{α}\left(- 2\right)dx + {∫}_{α}^{13}\left(- 1\right)dx + {∫}_{1/3}^{β}0dx + {∫}_{β}^{23}1 \cdot dx$

$= - 2\alpha - \left(\dfrac{1}{3} - \alpha\right) + \dfrac{2}{3} - \beta = - \alpha - \beta + \dfrac{1}{3}$

$y = 3x^{2} - 3x + 2$

When~$x \in \left(\dfrac{2}{3},1\right)$

$3x^{2} - 3x + 2 \in $\left(\dfrac{4}{3},$2)$

\left[3x^{2} - 3x + 2\right] = 1$

$∴ {I}_{2} = {∫}_{23}^{1}\left[3x^{2} - 3x + 2\right]dx = 1\left(1 - $\dfrac{2}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}

Hence~$I = \left(\dfrac{1}{3} - ( \alpha + \beta )) + \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) +$1$

=\dfrac{5}{3} -\left(\dfrac{7 - \sqrt{37}}{6} + \dfrac{7 - \sqrt{13}}{6})

=\dfrac{- 2}{3} + \dfrac{\sqrt{37} + \sqrt{13}}{6}= \dfrac{- 2}{3} + \dfrac{\sqrt{37} + \sqrt{13}}{6}

$= \dfrac{\sqrt{37} + \sqrt{13} - 4}{6}

questions.q: Let for $f(x)=7 \tan ^8 x+7 \tan ^6 x-3 \tan ^4 x-3 \tan ^2 x, \quad $\mathrm{I}$_1=\int_0^{\pi / 4} f(x) \mathrm{d} x$ and $\mathrm{I}_2=\int_0^{\pi / 4} x f(x) \mathrm{d} x$. Then $7 $\mathrm{I}$_1+12 $\mathrm{I}$_2$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} f(x) & =7 \tan ^8 x+7 \tan ^6 x-3 \tan ^4 x-3 \tan ^2 x \\ & =7 \tan ^6 x\left(1+\tan ^2 x\right)-3 \tan ^2 x\left(1+\tan ^2 x\right) \\ & =\left(7 \tan ^6 x-3 \tan ^2 x\right)\left(1+\tan ^2 x\right) \\ & =\left(7 \tan ^6 x-3 \tan ^2 x\right) \sec ^2 x \\ l_1= & \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} f(x) d x=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\left(7 \tan ^6 x-3 \tan ^2 x\right) \sec ^2 x d x \\ & =\left.\left(\frac{7 \tan ^7 x}{7}-\frac{3 \tan ^3 x}{3}\right)\right|_0 ^{\frac{\pi}{4}}=1-1=0\end{aligned}$\begin{aligned}
I_2= & \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} x f(x) d x=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} x\left(7 \tan ^6 x-3 \tan ^2 x\right) \sec ^2 x d x \\
& =\left.x\left(\tan ^7 x-\tan ^3 x\right)\right|_0 ^{\frac{\pi}{4}}-\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} 1 \cdot\left(\tan ^7 x-\tan ^3 x\right) d x \\
& =0-\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \tan ^3 x\left(\tan ^2 x-1\right)\left(\tan ^2 x+1\right) d x \\
& =\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\left(\tan ^3 x-\tan ^5 x\right) \sec ^2 x d x=\frac{\tan ^4 x}{4}-\left.\frac{\tan ^6 x}{6}\right|_0 ^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \\
& =\frac{1}{12}
\end{aligned}$$ Hence $7 I_1+12 I_2=1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

${∫}_{- \pi2}^{\pi2}\left(\dfrac{x^{2}\cos x}{1 + {π}^{x}} + \dfrac{1 + \sin^{2}x}{1 + e^{\sin^{2023}x}}\right)dx = \dfrac{π}{4}\left(\pi + \alpha\right) - 4$

Now let, ${I}_{1} = {∫}_{- \pi2}^{\pi2} \left(\dfrac{x^{2}\cos x}{1 + {π}^{x}}\right)dx . . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

Now using the property ${∫}_a^{b}f\left(x\right) d x = {∫}_a^{b}f\left(a + b - x\right) d x$ we get,

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {∫}_{- \pi2}^{\pi2} \left(\dfrac{x^{2}\cos x}{1 + {π}^{- x}}\right)dx . . . . . . . . \left(ii\right)$

Now adding above equations we get,

$⇒ 2{I}_{1} = 2{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\left(x^{2}\cos x\right)dx\left\${\text{as}{∫}_{- a$a}^{a}$f \left($x\right) d x = 2{∫}_{0}^{a}f\left($x\right) d x, $\ttext{if}f\left(x\right)\text{is even}\right

$⇒ {I}_{1} = ${x^{2}\left(\text{ \sin x }\right)}$_{0}^{\pi2} - {∫}_{0}^{\pi2}2x $\cdot$sinxdx$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = \dfrac{\pi2}{4} - \left[{- 2xcosx}_{0}^{\pi2} + {∫}_{0}^{\pi2}$2cosxdx\right]$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = \dfrac{\pi2}{4} -2$

Similarly solving, ${I}_{2} = {∫}_{- \pi2}^{\$pi2}\left(\dfrac{1 + \sin^{2}x}${1 + e^{\sin^{2023}x}}\right)dx$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = {∫}_{0}^{\$pi2} \left($1 + \sin^{2}x\right)dx$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = {∫}_{0}^{\$pi2}\left($1 + $\dfrac{1 - \cos 2x}{2}\right)$dx$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = $\dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\left($3 - \cos 2x\right)dx$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = $\dfrac{1}{2}{3x - \dfrac{\sin 2x}{2}}_{0}^{\pi2}

$⇒ {I}_{2} = $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}

$⇒ {I}_{1} + {I}_{2} = $\dfrac{\pi2}{4} -$2 + $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}

$⇒ $\dfrac{π}{4}\left(\pi +$3\right) - 2 = $\dfrac{π}{4}\left(\pi + \alpha\right) -$2$

$⇒ $\alpha =$3

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & 4 \int_0^1 \frac{1}{\sqrt{3+\mathrm{x}^2}+\sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2}} \mathrm{dx}-3 \ln \sqrt{3} \\ & =4 \int_0^1 \frac{\sqrt{3+\mathrm{x}^2}-\sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2}}{\left(3+\mathrm{x}^2\right)-\left(1-\mathrm{x}^2\right)} \mathrm{dx}-\frac{3}{2} \ln 3 \\ & = \\ & 2\left[\left\{\frac{\mathrm{x}}{2} \sqrt{3+\mathrm{x}^2}+\frac{3}{2} \ln \left(\mathrm{x}+\sqrt{3+\mathrm{x}^2}\right)\right\}_0^1\right. \\ & \left.\quad-\left\{\frac{\mathrm{x}}{2} \sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2}+\frac{1}{2} \ln \left(\mathrm{x}+\sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2}\right)\right\}_0^1\right]-\frac{3}{2} \ln 3\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}= & 2\left[\left\{\frac{1}{2} \sqrt{4}+\frac{3}{2} \ln (1+\sqrt{4})\right\}-\left\{0+\frac{3}{2} \ln \sqrt{3}\right\}\right. \\ & \left.-\left\{\frac{1}{2} \sqrt{2}+\frac{1}{2} \ln (1+\sqrt{2})\right\}+\left\{0+\frac{1}{2}(0)\right\}\right]-\frac{3}{2} \ln 3\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & =2\left[1+\frac{3}{2} \ln 3-\frac{3}{4} \ln 3-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{1}{2} \ln (1+\sqrt{2})\right]-\frac{3}{2} \ln 3 \\ & =2+3 \ln 3-\frac{3}{2} \ln 3-\sqrt{2}-\ln (1+\sqrt{2})-\frac{3}{2} \ln 3 \\ & =2-\sqrt{2}-\ln (1+\sqrt{2})\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let the function $f: \left[0, 2\right] \to \mathbb{R}$ be defined as~$f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}e^{min\left\{x^{2}, x - \left[x\right]\right\}}, & x \in [ 0, 1 ) \\ e  \left[x - \log_{\mathrm{e}}x\right], & x \in \left[$1, 2\right]\end{cases}\right,~where  \left[t\right]$~denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$. Then the value of the integral~${∫}_{0}^{2}xf\left(x\right)dx$& is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \left\{$\begin{cases}e^{min\left\{x^{2}, x - \left[x\right]\right\}}, & x \in [ 0, 1 ) \\ e \left[x - \log_{\mathrm{e}}x\right], & x \in \left[1, 2\right]\end{cases}$\right
$⇒ $f\left($x\right) = \left\${$\begin{cases}e^{x2} & x \in [ 0, 1 ) \\ e, & x \in \left[1, 2\right]\end{cases}$\right

As~$x - \ln x \in [ 1, 2 )$ for $x \in [ 1, 2 ]$, so\left[$x - \ln x\right] = 1$~and~$x - \left[$x\right] = \left\{x\right\}$, so~$x \in \left($0, 1\right), x^{2} < \left\{x\right\}$

Now solving the integral we get,${∫}_{0}^{2}xf\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{1}x \cdot e^{x2}dx + {∫}_{1}^{2}x \cdot edx$

Now in first integral, let~$x^{2} = t ⇒ 2xdx = dt$~we get,

$⇒ {∫}_{0}^{2}xf\left(x\right) = \left[\dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}e^{t}dt\right] + {e \cdot \dfrac{x2}{2}}_{1}^{2}$

$⇒ {∫}_{0}^{2}xf\left(x\right) = \left(\dfrac{e - 1}{2}\right) + \dfrac{3e}{2}$

$⇒ {∫}_{0}^{2}xf\left(x\right) = 2e - \dfrac{1}{2}$

$

questions.q: The value of the integral ${∫}_{- 2}^{2}\dfrac{\left|x^{3} + x\right|}{\left(e^{x\left|x\right|} + 1\right)}dx$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{\left|x^{3} + x\right|}{\left(e^{x\left|x\right|} + 1\right)}dx$

and ${∫}_{- 2}^{2}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{0}^{2}\left(f\left(x\right) + f\left(- x\right)\right)dx$

$= {∫}_{0}^{2}\left(\dfrac{\left|x^{3} + x\right|}{\left(e^{x\left|x\right|} + 1\right)} + \dfrac{\left|- x^{3} - x\right|}{\left(e^{- x\left|- x\right|} + 1\right)}\right)dx$

$= {∫}_{0}^{2}\left(\dfrac{\left|x^{3} + x\right|}{\left(e^{x\left|x\right|} + 1\right)} + \dfrac{\left|x^{3} + x\right|}{\left(e^{- x\left|x\right|} + 1\right)}\right)dx$

$= {∫}_{0}^{2}\left(\dfrac{x^{3} + x}{\left(e^{x^{2}} + 1\right)} + \dfrac{x^{3} + x}{\left(e^{- x^{2}} + 1\right)}\right)dx$

$I = {∫}_{0}^{2}\left(\dfrac{x^{3} + x}{1 + e^{x^{2}}} + \dfrac{e^{x^{2}}\left(x^{3} + x\right)}{1 + e^{x^{2}}}\right)dx$

$= {∫}_{0}^{2}\left(x^{3} + x\right)dx$

$= {\left[\dfrac{x^{4}}{4} + \dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\right]}_{0}^{2}$

$= 4 + 2 = 6$

questions.q: Let $f: R \to R$ be defined $f\left(x\right) = ae^{2x} + be^{x} + cx$. If $f ( 0 ) = - 1, f^{'}\left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}2\right) = 21$ and ${∫}_{0}^{\log 4}\left(f\left(x\right) - cx\right)dx = \dfrac{39}{2}$, then the value of $| a + b + c |$ equals:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$

Given: $f\left(x\right) = ae^{2x} + be^{x} + cx, f\left(0\right) = - 1, f^{'}\left(\log 2\right) = 21, {∫}_{0}^{\log 4} \left($f \left(x\right) - cx\right) = \dfrac{39}{2}$

$⇒ f\left(0\right) = a + b = - 1 . . . \left(i\right)$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(x\right) = 2ae^{2x} + be^{x} + c$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(\log 2\right) = 2a \left(4\right) + b \left($2\right) + c = 21$

$⇒ 8a + 2b + c = 21 . . . \left($ii\right)$

Also, ${∫}_{0}^{\log 4}\left($ae^{2x} + be^{x} + cx - cx\right) = $\dfrac{39}{2}

$⇒ {∫}_{0}^{\log 4}\left($ae^{2x} + be^{x}\right) = $\dfrac{39}{2}

$⇒ ${\dfrac{ae^{2x}}{2} +be^{x}}_{0}^{\log 4} = \dfrac{39}{2}

$⇒ $\dfrac{ae^{2\log 4}}{2} +$be^{\log 4} - $\dfrac{a}{2} -$b = $\dfrac{39}{2}

$⇒ $\dfrac{15a}{2} +$3b = $\dfrac{39}{2}

$⇒ 15a + 6b = 39$

Using equation \left(i\right)$,

$⇒ 15a + 6\left(-1 - a\right) = 39$

$⇒ 15a - 6 - 6a = 39$

$⇒ 9a = 45$

$⇒ a = 5$

$⇒ b = - 1 - 5 = - 6$

$⇒ c = 21 - 8a - 2b$

$⇒ c = 21 - 40 + 12 = - 7$

$⇒ c = - 7$

$⇒ \left|a + b + c\right| = 8$

$

questions.q: Let $g\left(t\right) = {∫}_{- \pi / 2}^{\pi / 2}\left(cos\dfrac{π}{4}t + f\left(x\right)\right)dx,$~where~$f\left(x\right) = \log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(x + \sqrt{x^{2} + 1}\right), x \in \mathbb{R} .$ Then which one of the following is correct?
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$We have,

$f\left(x\right) = \log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(x + \sqrt{x^{2} + 1}\right), x \in R$

$⇒ f \left(x\right) = \log_{\mathrm{e}} \left(\dfrac{ \left($x + $\sqrt{x^{2} + 1}\right)\left($x - $\sqrt{x^{2} + 1}\right)}${x - \sqrt{x^{2} + 1}}$\right)$

$⇒ f \left($x\right) = \log_{\mathrm{e}} $\left(\dfrac{- 1}{x - \sqrt{x^{2} + 1}})

$⇒ f \left(x\right) = \log_{\mathrm{e}} \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x^{2} + 1} - x})$

$⇒ f \left(-$x\right) = \log_{\mathrm{e}} \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x^{2} + 1} + x}\right)$

$⇒ f\left(-x\right) = \log_{\mathrm{e}} $\left(\sqrt{x^{2} + 1} +x)- 1$

$⇒ $f \left(-x\right) = - \log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\sqrt{x^{2} + 1} +$x)$

$⇒ f \left(-x\right) = - f \left($x\right)$

Hence,~$f \left($x\right)$~is an odd function.

Now,

g\left($t\right) = {∫}_{- \pi/ 2}$^{\pi$/ $2}\lleft(cos\dfrac{π}{4}t + f\left(x\right))dx$

$⇒ g\left(t\right) = cos\dfrac{π}{4}t{∫}_{- \pi/ 2}^{\pi/ 2}1dx + {∫}_{- \pi/ 2}^{\pi/ 2}f\left(x\right)dx$

$⇒ g\left(t\right) = \pi cos\dfrac{π}{4}t + {∫}_{- $\pi$/ $2}^{\pi$/ 2}f \left($x\right)dx$

$⇒ $g\left($t\right) = \$picos\dfrac{π}{4}$t + 0$

$∵ $f\left($x\right)$~is an odd function.

$∴ $g\left($1\right) = $\dfrac{π}{2}$⇒ $\ssqrt{2}g\left(1\right) = \pi$

$g\left(0\right) = \pi$

$

questions.q: The integral $\int_0^{\pi / 4} \frac{136 \sin x}{3 \sin x+5 \cos x} d x$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & I=\int_0^{\pi / 4} \frac{136 \sin x}{3 \sin x+5 \cos x} d x \\ & 136 \sin x=A(3 \sin x+5 \cos x)+B(3 \cos x-5 \sin x) \\ & 136=3 A-5 B...(i) \\ & 0=5 A+3 B...(ii)\end{aligned}$\begin{aligned} & 3 \mathrm{~B}=-5 \mathrm{~A} \Rightarrow \mathrm{B}=-\frac{5}{3} \mathrm{~A} \\ & 136=3 \mathrm{~A}-5\left(-\frac{5}{3} \mathrm{~A}\right) \\ & 136=3 \mathrm{~A}+\frac{25}{3} \mathrm{~A} \\ & 136=\frac{34 \mathrm{~A}}{3} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{A}=\frac{136 \times 3}{34}=12 \\ & \mathrm{~B}=\frac{-5}{3}(12)=-20\end{aligned}$\begin{aligned} & I=\int_0^{\pi / 4} \frac{A(3 \sin x+5 \cos x)}{3 \sin x+5 \cos x}+\int_0^{\pi / 4} \frac{B(3 \cos x-5 \sin x)}{3 \sin x+5 \cos x} \\ & =A(x)_0^{\pi / 4}+B[\ln (3 \sin x+5 \cos x)]_0^{\pi / 4} \\ & =12\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)-20 \ln \left(\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{5}{\sqrt{2}}\right)-\ln (0+5) \\ & =3 \pi-20 \ln 4 \sqrt{2}+20 \ln 5 \\ & =3 \pi-20 \times \frac{5}{2} \ln 2+20 \ln 5 \\ & =3 \pi-50 \ln 2+20 \ln 5\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $f\left(a + b + 1 - x\right) = f\left(x\right),$ for all $x,$ where $a$ and $b$ are fixed positive real numbers, then $\dfrac{1}{a + b}\mathop{∫}_a^{b}x\left(f\left(x\right) + f\left(x + 1\right)\right)dx$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
I = 1\left(a + b\right)\mathop{∫}_a^{b}x \left[f \left($x\right) + f \left(x + 1\right)\right]dx \ldots \left(1\right)$
$x \to a + b - x$
$I = 1\left(a + b\right)\mathop{∫}_a^{b}\left(a + b - x\right)\lleft[f\left(a + b - x\right) + \left(a + b + 1 - x\right)\right]dx$
$I = 1 \left($a + b\right)\mathop{∫}_a^{b}a \left(a + b - x\right) \left[f \left($x + 1\right) + $f\left($x\right)dx\right] \ldots \left($2\right)$
$∵$~Keeping~$x \to x + 1$~in given relation
\left($1\right) + \left($2\right)$
$2I = \mathop{∫}_a^{b}\lleft[f\left(x + 1\right) + f\left(x\right)] d x$
$2I = \mathop{∫}_a^{b}f\left(x + 1\right)dx + \mathop{∫}_a^{b}f\left(x\right)dx$
$\mathop{∫}_a^{b}f\left(a + b + 1 - x\right)dx + \mathop{∫}_a^{b}f\left(x\right)dx$
$2I = 2\mathop{∫}_a^{b}f\left(x\right)dx$
$I = \mathop{∫}_a^{b}f\left(x\right)dx$
Put $x = t + 1 ⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{a - 1}^{b - 1}f\left(t + 1\right)dt = \mathop{∫}_{a - 1}^{b - 1}f\left(x + 1\right)dx$

questions.q: Let [x]& denote the greatest integer $\le x$. Consider the function $f ( x ) = max\left\{x^{2}, 1 + [ x ]\right\}$. Then the value of the integral ${∫}_{0}^{2}f ( x ) dx$ is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Plotting the diagram of the given function& $f ( x ) = max\left\{x^{2}, 1 + [ x ]\right\}$~we get,

Now when~$x \in [ 0, 1 ) ⇒ f\left(x\right) = 1$

When~$x \in [ 1, \sqrt{2} ) ⇒ f\left(x\right) = 2$

And when~$x \in \left[\sqrt{2}, 2\right] ⇒ f\left(x\right) = x^{2}$

So, from above diagram area can be calculated as,

$A = {∫}_{0}^{1}1 . dx + {∫}_{1}^{2}2dx + {∫}_{2}^{2}x^{2}dx$

$⇒ A = 1 + 2\sqrt{2} - 2 + \dfrac{8}{3} - \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}$

$⇒ A = \dfrac{5}{3} + \dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{3}$

questions.q: Let $(a, b)$ be the point of intersection of the curve $x^2=2 y$ and the straight line $y-2 x-6=0$ in the second quadrant. Then the integral $I=\int_a^b \frac{9 x^2}{1+5^x} d x$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & x^2=2 y & y=2 x+6 \\ & x^2=4 x+12\end{aligned}$
\left.x^2-4 x-12=0 \Rightarrow \begin{gathered}x=6 \\ y=18\end{gathered} \right\rvert\, \begin{gathered}\text { if } x=-2 \\ y=2\end{gathered}$
$\therefore(6,18) \ \text{ and } (-2,2)$
Here $(6,18)$ Rejected because $(a, b)$ lies in $2^{\text {nd }}$ quadrant
$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \mathrm{a}=-2 & \mathrm{~b}=2 \\ & \therefore \mathrm{I}=\int_{-2}^2 \frac{9 \mathrm{x}^2}{1+5^{\mathrm{x}}} \mathrm{dx}=\int_{-2}^2 \frac{9 \cdot 5^{\mathrm{x}} \cdot \mathrm{x}^2}{1+5^{\mathrm{x}}} \mathrm{dx} \\ & \therefore 2 \mathrm{I}=\int_{-2}^2 9 \mathrm{x}^2 \mathrm{dx}=18 \int_0^2 \mathrm{x}^2 \mathrm{dx}=18\left(\frac{\mathrm{x}^3}{3}\right)_0^2 \\ & 2 \mathrm{I}=48 \\ & \therefore \mathrm{I}=24\end{aligned}

questions.q: The value of the integral ${∫}_{- 1}^{1}\log \left(x + \sqrt{x^{2} + 1}\right)dx$ is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let $I = {∫}_{- 1}^{1}\log \left(x + \sqrt{x^{2} + 1}\right)dx$

Consider $f\left(x\right) = \log \left(x + \sqrt{x^{2} + 1}\right)$

Now, $f\left(- x\right) = \log \left(- x + \sqrt{1 + x^{2}}\right)$

$⇒ f\left(- x\right) = - \log \left(x + \sqrt{1 + x^{2}}\right)$

$⇒ f\left(- x\right) = - f\left(x\right)$

So, $f\left(x\right)$ is an odd function.

$∴ I = 0$

questions.q: The value of ${∫}_{0}^{π}\dfrac{e^{\cos x}\sin x}{\left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right)\left(e^{\cos x} + e^{- \cos x}\right)}dx$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{π}\dfrac{\sin x ⋅ e^{\cos x}}{ \left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right)\left(e^{\cos x} + e^{- \cos x}\right)}dx . . . \left(i\right)$

Using property of integral~$\mathop{∫ f}_a^{b} \left($a + b - x\right) = \mathop{∫}_a^{b}f\left($x\right)$

we get~$I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{π}\dfrac{\sin x ⋅ e^{- \cos x}}{ \left($1 + \cos^{2}x\right)\left(e^{- \cos x} + e^{\cos x}\right)}dx . . . \left(ii\right)$

Adding equation~ \left(i\right)$~&~ \left($ii\right)$~we get

$2I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{π}\sin x\left($1 + \cos^{2}x\right) ⋅ \left($e^{\cos x} + e^{- \cos x}\right)e^{\cos x} + e^{- \cos x}dx$

$2I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{π}$\dfrac{\sin x}{1 + \cos^{2}x}$dx$~ ~$⇒ 2I = 2\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}$\dfrac{\sin x}{1 + \cos^{2}x}$dx$

Let~$\cos x = t ⇒ - sinxdx = dt$

$I = - \mathop{∫}_{1}^{0}$\dfrac{dt}{1 + t^{2}}$⇒ I = - {\tan^{- 1}t}_{1}^{0} = - \left[0 - \dfrac{π}{4}\right]$~$= \dfrac{π}{4}$

questions.q: The value $9{∫}_{0}^{9}\left[\sqrt{\dfrac{10x}{x + 1}}\right]dx$, where $t$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$, is _____.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let,

$I = {∫}_{0}^{9} \left[\sqrt{\dfrac{10x}{x + 1}}dx\right]$

The square of integers are $0, 1, 4, 9, . . .$

$⇒ 0 = \dfrac{10x}{x + 1}⇒ x = 0 . . . \left(i\right)$

$⇒ 1 = $\dfrac{10x}{x + 1}$⇒ x + 1 = 10x$

$⇒ x = $\dfrac{1}{9} . . . \left(ii\right)$

$⇒ 4 = \dfrac{10x}{x + 1}⇒ 4x + 4 = 10x$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{2}{3} . . . \left(iii\right)$

$⇒ 9 = \dfrac{10x}{x + 1}⇒ 9x + 9 = 10x$

$⇒ x = 9 . . . \left(iv\right)$

Now, from the above equations using the law ${∫}_a^{b}f\left(x\right) d x = {∫}_a^{c}f\left(x\right) d x + {∫}_c^{d}f\left(x\right) d x + {∫}_d^{b}f\left(x\right) d x$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{19}\left(0\right)dx + {∫}_{19}^{23}\left(1\right)dx + {∫}_{23}^{9} \left($2\right)dx$

$⇒ I = $\dfrac{2}{3} - \dfrac{1}{9} +2\left($9 - $\dfrac{2}{3}\right)

$⇒ I = $\dfrac{155}{9}

$⇒ 9I = 155$

$

questions.q: Let $f$~be a differentiable function satisfying $f \left($x\right) = $\dfrac{2}{3}{∫}_{0}^{3}$f  \left(\dfrac{{λ}^{2}x}{3}\right)d\lambda, x > 0$~and $f\left(1\right) = \sqrt{3}.$If $y = f\left(x\right)$~passes through the point  \left(\alpha,$6\right)$, then \alpha is equal to _______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2}{3}{∫}_{0}^{3}f\left(\dfrac{{λ}^{2}x}{3}\right)d\lambda$

Now let~$\dfrac{{λ}^{2}x}{3} = t$

$⇒ \dfrac{2\lambdax}{3}d\lambda = dt$

$⇒ d\lambda = \dfrac{3}{2} \cdot \dfrac{1\sqrt{x}}{x \cdot \sqrt{3}\sqrt{t}}dt$

$⇒ d\lambda = \dfrac{3}{2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{x} \cdot \dfrac{dt}{t}$

So,~$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{x}{∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{f\left(t\right)}{t}dt$

$\sqrt{x}f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{f\left(t\right)}{t}dt$

Now differentiating both side we get,

$⇒ \sqrt{x} \cdot f^{'}\left(x\right) + \dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{2\sqrt{x}} = \dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{x}$

$⇒ \sqrt{x} \cdot f^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{2\sqrt{x}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{y} = \dfrac{dx}{2x}$

Now integrating both side we get,

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{dy}{y} = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{2x}$

$⇒ \ln y = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln x + lnc$

Given~$f\left(1\right) = \sqrt{3}$, so~$⇒ ln\sqrt{3} = 0 + lnc$

$⇒ c = \sqrt{3}$

So,~$f \left(x\right) = $\sqrt{3x}

Now given $f\left(x\right)$~is passing through~ \left(\alpha,6\right)$,

So~$f\left(\alpha\right) =6 ⇒ 36 = 3\alpha$

$⇒ \alpha =12$

$

questions.q: Let& $F:  \left[3, 5\right] \to R$~be a twice differentiable~function on \left(3, 5\right)$ such that~$F\left(x\right) = e^{- x}{∫}_{3}^{x}\left(3t^{2} + 2t + 4F^{'}\left(t\right)\right)dt .$~If~$F^{'}\left(4\right) = $\dfrac{\alphae^{β} - 224}{\left(e^{β} - 4\right)2},~then $\alpha + \beta is$equal to _____.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,&

$F\left(x\right) = e^{- x}{∫}_{3}^{x}\left(3t^{2} + 2t + 4F^{'}\left(t\right)\right)dt .$

So,~$F\left(3\right) = e^{- 3}{∫}_{3}^{3}\left(3t^{2} + 2t + 4F^{'}\left(t\right)\right)dt .$~

$⇒ F\left(3\right) = 0$

Again,~$e^{x}F\left(x\right) = {∫}_{3}^{x}\left(3t^{2} + 2t + 4F^{'}\left(t\right)\right)dt$

Differentiate both sides

$⇒ e^{x}F \left(x\right) + e^{x}F^{'} \left($x\right) = 3x^{2} + 2x + 4F^{'}\left($x\right)$~(Newton Leibnitz Theorem for Definite Integral)

$⇒ \left(e^{x} - 4\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} +$e^{x}y = \left(3x^{2} + 2x\right)$~(Use~$y = F \left(x\right)$)

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} +e^{x} \left($e^{x} - 4\right)y = \left($3x^{2} + 2x\right)\left($e^{x} - 4\right)$

Here, integrating factor is~$e^{∫ $\dfrac{ex}{e^{x} - 4}$dx} = $e^{\ln \left(e^{x} - 4\right)} =$e^{x} - 4$

So, the solution is~

$y $\cdot \left($e^{x} - 4\right) = ∫ \left($3x^{2} + 2x\right)dx + c$

$⇒ y $\cdot \left($e^{x} - 4\right) = \left($x^{3} + x^{2}\right) + c$

Put~$x = 3, y = 0 ⇒ c = - 36$

So,~$F \left($x\right) = \left($x^{3} + x^{2} - 36\right)\left(e^{x} - 4\right)$

$⇒ F^{'}\left(x\right) = $\dfrac{\left(3x^{2} + 2x\right)\left(e^{x} - 4\right) - \left(x^{3} + x^{2} - 36\right)e^{x}}{\left(e^{x} - 4\right)2}

Now put value of $x = 4$~we will get

$F^{'}\left(4\right) = $\dfrac{\left(3\left(4\right)2 + 2\left(4\right)\right)\left(e^{4} - 4\right) - \left(\left(4\right)3 + \left(4\right)2 - 36\right)e^{4}}{\left(e^{4} - 4\right)2} = \dfrac{12e^{4} - 224}{\left(e^{4} - 4\right)2}

So,~$\alpha =12 \text{ and } \beta =4$

Hence,~$\alpha + \beta =16$

$

questions.q: Let& ${f}_{n} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\left(\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}\sin^{k - 1}x\right)\left(\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n} ( 2k - 1 ) \sin^{k - 1}x\right)cosxdx, n \in \mathbb{N} .$~Then ${f}_{21} - {f}_{20}$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

${f}_{n} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}\left(\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}\sin^{k - 1}x\right)\left(\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n} ( 2k - 1 ) \sin^{k - 1}x\right)cosxdx$

Now let,~$\sin x = t$

$⇒ cosxdx = dt$

So,~${f}_{n} = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n} ( t{)}^{k - 1}\right)\left(\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n} ( 2k - 1 ) ( t{)}^{k - 1}\right)dt$

$⇒ {f}_{n} = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(1 + t + t^{2} . . . . + t^{n - 1}\right)\left(1 + 3t + 5t^{2} + . . . . . + \left(2n - 1\right)t^{n - 1}\right)dt$

Now multiply and divide by~$\sqrt{t}$~we get,

$⇒ {f}_{n} = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(t^{\dfrac{1}{2}} + t^{\dfrac{3}{2}} + t\dfrac{5}{2} . . . . + t^{\dfrac{2n - 1}{2}}\right)\sqrt{t}\left(1 + 3t + 5t^{2} + . . . . . + \left(2n - 1\right)t^{n - 1}\right)dt$

$⇒ {f}_{n} = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(t\dfrac{1}{2} + t\dfrac{3}{2} + t\dfrac{5}{2} . . . . + t\dfrac{2n - 1}{2}\right)\left(t\dfrac{- 1}{2} + 3t\dfrac{1}{2} + 5t\dfrac{3}{2} + . . . . . + \left(2n - 1\right)t\dfrac{2n - 3}{2}\right)dt$

Now let~$t\dfrac{1}{2} + t\dfrac{3}{2} + t\dfrac{5}{2} . . . . + t\dfrac{2n - 1}{2} = z$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}\left(t\dfrac{- 1}{2} + 3t\dfrac{1}{2} + 5t\dfrac{3}{2} + . . . . . + \left(2n - 1\right)t\dfrac{2n - 3}{2}\right)dt = dz$

Hence, the integral becomes,

$⇒ {f}_{n} = 2{∫}_{0}^{n}zdz$

$⇒ {f}_{n} = {z^{2}}_{0}^{n} = n^{2}$

Hence,~${f}_{21} - {f}_{20} = {21}^{2} - {20}^{2} = 41$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$f(x)=\frac{1}{e^{x-1}}=e^{1-x}$
f(x)=2f(x)=1
$\frac{1}{\mathrme^{x-1}}=$2x=1
x=1-\ln 2

$f(0)=e^1=2.71$

$=2(1-\ell \operatorname{n} 2-0)+1(1-1+\ln 2)+0$
